🏔️ Darjeeling or Sikkim? Here's how to decide - once and for all.

Both are in the Eastern Himalayas. Both are spectacular. But they give you very different experiences.

Choose DARJEELING if you want:
→ Colonial tea gardens and the famous Toy Train (UNESCO heritage)
→ Tiger Hill sunrise with Kanchenjunga views at 8,400 ft
→ A relaxed hill station with markets, cafes, and walking culture
→ Good infrastructure, easy for first-time travellers
→ Himalayan Mountaineering Institute, Padmaja Naidu Zoo

🏔️ Choose SIKKIM if you want:
→ Yumthang Valley (Valley of Flowers) at 12,000 ft
→ The thrill of North Sikkim Lachung, Chungthang, Gurudongmar Lake
→ Buddhist monasteries - Rumtek, Pemayangtse, Enchey
→ More raw adventure, higher altitude, offbeat experiences
→ Waterfalls every 10 km - Naga Falls, Bhim Nala, Khangchendzongha Falls

Can't choose? Don't.
Most of our travelers combine both: 4 nights in Darjeeling + 4 nights in Sikkim. You get the colonial charm AND the mountain adventure.

Best times for either are March–June and September–November.

Here's the 4-day plan:

📍 Day 1: Arrive → check in → Fort Aguada sunset
A 17th-century Portuguese fort. Panoramic views of the Arabian Sea. The kind of view that makes you forget you work.

Baga Beach morning → Anjuna Flea Market → Chapora Fort (yes, the Dil Chahta Hai fort) for the most spectacular sunset in North Goa.

Old Goa churches → Panjim lanes → Fontainhas (Latin Quarter) → riverfront dinner on Mandovi.

Best beaches in Kerala - Varkala, Kovalam & Alleppey
Kerala has 600 km of coastline. These are the 3 beaches actually worth your time.

Varkala - the cliff beach
Red laterite cliffs towering over the Arabian Sea. This is the one that doesn't look real in photos. The northern end is safest for swimming. Surf schools available. Best for: couples, backpackers, those who want something dramatic.

Kovalam - the most complete beach destination
Three connected bays: Lighthouse Beach (most popular), Hawa Beach (calmer), and Samudra Beach. Parasailing, catamaran rides, ayurvedic spas, and a solid lineup of restaurants. Best for: first-timers, families, those who want everything in one place.

Alleppey - not a beach but a must
Technically a backwater destination, but the combination of beach + houseboat + lagoon makes it essential on any Kerala trip. Best for: houseboat experience, couples, anyone who wants to slow down.

When to go:
→ October to March: ideal — dry, calm sea, swimming-safe
→ June to September: no swimming, but the landscape is extraordinary and Ayurveda treatments are considered best this season
→ April–May: hot but good for domestic travellers

Despite sending them the link of the Korean consulate website specifically stating the above rule for NRIs they refused to acknowledge that any such rule exists and that we have to apply on Cambodia. I also informed them that we have visited Korean Embassy in Cambodia and they told us to apply in India due the 2 year residency rule. Hana travels refused to accept it. Their "seniors" know better.

Hana travels also told me that in any case my husband's passport is issued in Uttar Pradesh. So they cannot take his application because it doesn't come under their "jurisdiction" and my husband will have to apply from Delhi. To which i asked them you can take my application as my passport is issued in Mumbai and my permanent address is also from Mumbai. To which they tell me that no, my birthplace is Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh so they cannot take my application as well. Very confused, I asked them what happens to my son's application since he was born in Seoul, South Korea and his passport was also issued in Seoul. They never answered that question. With their logic, i need to take his passport to Seoul to apply for visa for South Korea. An agency who specifically does South Korean visashas zero knowledge about how this works.

When i asked them to please connect with the consulate and clarify because i am 100% sure i cannot apply in Cambodia and i need to apply in India. They said they have consulted their "seniors" and yet again, their seniors know better. Hana travels sent me a link of the consulate website and asked me to contact them myself. A simple phone call also was too much for them to do because too arrogant to admit they have no idea what i am talking about.

I emailed the consulate, and i got a response withing minutes that i need to apply in India. I have shared the screenshot for the "learned seniors" information. No reply to that as well.

The attitude with which Hana travels spoke to me when they themselves were unaware of the rule was rather amusing. An honest hardworking agency would take it upon themselves to find out about a rule if it's come to their attention for the first time. Rather than trying to make me look dumb and do the research they are supposed to do.

I will obviously not be using their service again. And would advice you not to either. Because their lack of experience and commitment to providing basic service will get your visa rejected.

If you only had taken the same amount of time as you took to write this response in finding out what needs to be done in our case, you would be professional. We have engaged another agency who will be finding everything out  for us rather than giving us a standard response that they have limitations and restrictions and jurisdictions and that you can't do it. It was me who had to get confirmation that i need to apply from India. So please dont try to mask your unprofessionalism.
